item.title: Minister Wasserlauf: We received reports of Ra’am envelopes with money outside polling stations
item.description:
Minister Yitzhak Wasserlauf said in an interview with Kan News on Reshet Bet that Otzma Yehudit received dozens of reports and video recordings on election day alleging irregularities at polling stations, including claims that money was distributed in exchange for votes for Ra’am.
Wasserlauf described a report received from a party activist at the Beit al-Hikma school in Rahat, according to which a sheikh and several other people were sitting outside the polling station. Ra’am envelopes containing money were reportedly seen at the scene, along with people carrying long-barreled firearms.
He said the materials were forwarded to the relevant authorities in real time, and MK Yitzhak Kroizer contacted Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Solberg regarding the matter.

item.title: Businessman Alexander Blok extradited from Israel to US
item.description:
Alexander Blok (Gurvitz), an Israeli and Russian citizen, was extradited from Israel to the US early Thursday morning to face charges of fraud and computer-related offenses, transferring stolen goods, and money laundering.
According to the allegations, Blok exploited a security vulnerability in the Nomad cryptocurrency platform in August 2022 to withdraw tokens worth approximately $2.8 million. He allegedly converted the tokens and transferred the funds between digital wallets to conceal their origin.
Blok was arrested at Ben-Gurion Airport in May 2025 while on his way to Russia. His extradition proceeded after the Supreme Court rejected his appeal, and his subsequent request for a further hearing was also denied.

item.title: New invasive ant species detected in Israel for the first time in Haifa
item.description:
The Environmental Protection Ministry has identified the African big-headed ant for the first time in the Neve Sha’anan neighborhood of Haifa. The species is considered one of the world’s 100 most harmful invasive species. Reports of its presence in other parts of the city are also being investigated.
The ministry is working with the Haifa Municipality, the Israel Nature and Parks Authority, and Tel Aviv University to expand monitoring efforts and examine pest-control solutions suited to Israeli conditions.
“The public is asked to report any suspected sightings to help map infestation hotspots and prevent the spread of this invasive species," the ministry said.

item.title: Turkish report: Erdogan discusses Middle East developments with Trump

item.title: 90.4% of votes counted: No change in bloc distribution
item.description:
According to the partial official results of the elections for Israel's 26th Knesset, updated at 1:18 a.m., with approximately 90.4% of the votes counted, the distribution of seats remains unchanged. The current coalition holds 53 seats, the opposition bloc 48, and the Arab parties 19.
Likud leads with 26 seats, followed by Yashar with 21. The Joint List and Together each receive 12 seats, the Democrats eight, while Ra'am, Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism, Otzma Yehudit, and Shas each receive seven. The joint Religious Zionist-Zehut list receives six seats.
The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.63% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.6%.
